info.title: MJOLNIR Hub API
info.description: Open API for the MJOLNIR mod platform for Halo Campaign Evolved. Reads are public and unauthenticated. Browser sessions use Discord OAuth with an HttpOnly cookie; third-party tools authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer mjc_…` API keys carrying scopes (mods:read, mods:write, ratings:write, comments:write), minted at /account/api-keys. Desktop clients with no browser session pair instead: /auth/device/start, show the user the code, and poll /auth/device/token for a scoped key. Any authenticated write may additionally answer 401 (no identity), 403 (missing scope), or 429 (per-subject hourly write budget) with the standard Error shape.

avatar_url.description: Discord CDN avatar, when the user has one.

device_code.description: Secret for polling. Never display it.

scopes.description: What approval will grant — echoed back so a client can show it too.

key.description: The minted API key, returned exactly once — on the first poll after approval. Store it; it is not retrievable again.

scopes.description: What the key carries. Sent with the key so a client can check it got what it asked for instead of failing later at the write.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; null when exhausted.

type.description: Trust tier. `content` mods are inert game data and open to community upload. `script` (UE4SS Lua) and `native` (DLL) mods can execute code, so they ship exclusively from the mjolnir-core repository's reviewed, signed CI releases.

sha256.description: Hash of the release archive; verify after download.

signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature over the lowercase hex `sha256`, made with the platform release key (keys/mod-signing.pub). Present on signed script/native releases; null for community content uploads, whose integrity rests on `sha256` plus the upload scan. Clients that know the key must reject a release whose signature is present and wrong.

build_min.description: Oldest game build this release is declared compatible with.

published_by.description: Account that created this release; null for releases predating attribution.

signer_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the author signing key whose signature verified at publish. Distinct from `signature`, which is the platform key over the archive hash; this one is the author's own key over the archive contents (docs/mod_signing_design.md).

signer_key_revoked.description: True when the author's signing key has been revoked since publish.

chunk_count.description: IoStore chunks this release claims, once scanned.

published_by.description: Account that created this release; null for releases predating attribution.

signer_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the author key whose signature verified at publish, if any.

signer_key_revoked.description: True when the signing key has been revoked since this release published.

chunk_count.description: IoStore chunks the uploaded containers actually claim — measured by the scanner, not declared by the author.

DeclaredChanges.description: The archive's declared change list; null when it carried none.

before.description: The shipped value at export time, when it resolved.

shared_chunks.description: How many IoStore chunk IDs both releases claim.

pairs.description: Every conflicting pair among the requested releases. Empty means the set installs cleanly in any order.

sample_chunk_ids.description: Up to 10 shared chunk IDs, hex-encoded 12-byte identifiers.

release_ids.description: Releases a client intends to install together.

mod_id.description: The mod this belongs to; null for a tool preview.

tool_slug.description: The tool this belongs to; null for a mod's gallery item.

url.description: Where the file is served from.

status.description: Moderation state. Listings only include non-approved items for their own uploader; everyone else sees approved media only.

uploader.description: Display name of whoever submitted this item.

uploader_id.description: The submitter's user id, so a client can tell whose items carry controls without matching on display names.

mine.description: The caller's own score, when signed in and rated.

author.description: Null when the comment was deleted.

author_id.description: The author's user id, so a client can tell whose comments carry a delete button without matching on display names. Null when deleted.

fingerprint.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of the raw public key.

public_key.description: Raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, base64. The private key never leaves the device.

key_prefix.description: For telling keys apart; not the key.

key.description: The full key. Shown exactly once — store it now.

open_reporters.description: Distinct accounts currently holding open reports against it.

owner.description: What it was submitted to, and where that lives on the site.

get.description: Redirects the browser to Discord's consent screen. Pass `next` to return to a specific page after login.

500.description: OAuth is not configured on this deployment.

get.description: Discord redirects here; on success a session cookie is set.
Resolves either credential: the browser session cookie, or a Bearer API key. Desktop clients that paired a key ask this to find out whose account they are acting as.

post.description: Returns a short `user_code` to show the user and a secret `device_code` to poll with. Send the user to `verification_url` to approve. Codes live for 10 minutes.

client_name.description: Shown on the approval page so the user knows what they are approving.

scopes.description: What to ask for. Omit for read, rate and comment — what pairing granted before scopes were requestable. Ask for the narrowest set that works: the user sees this list.

post.summary: Poll a pairing for its key
post.description: Answers `pending` until the user decides. The first poll after approval carries the key and is the only one that does.

post.summary: Approve or deny a pairing code
post.description: Called from a signed-in browser session. Approving mints an API key carrying the scopes the client asked for at handshake time — expiring in 180 days, or 90 if it can publish — which the waiting client collects on its next poll. Only cookie sessions may approve — a key cannot pair another device.

404.description: No such code, or it expired.

get.description: Lets the approval page name the client, and say what it is asking for, before the user commits. Returns nothing that helps an attacker: the client name is a label the client chose for itself, and the scopes are what it would be granted anyway.

key_ttl_days.description: How long the minted key would last. Served rather than assumed so the approval page cannot promise a lifetime the mint no longer honours.

schema.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.

parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.
parameters.name: cursor

post.description: Creates a draft `content` mod owned by the signed-in user. Script and native mods cannot be created here; they ship from the mjolnir-core repository's release pipeline.

get.summary: Published releases of a mod, newest first

201.description: The pending release; upload its archive next.

403.description: Not the owner, or not a content mod.

put.description: Raw zip bytes, at most 50 MiB. Re-uploading while pending or rejected replaces the archive and resets the release to pending.

200.description: Stored; call /complete to scan and publish.

post.summary: Scan the uploaded archive and publish or reject

200.description: Scan finished; status says whether it published.

409.description: No archive uploaded, or already decided.

get.summary: What a release declares it changes
get.description: The change list the archive carried (changes.json): tag edits as shipped → modded values, replaced textures and scripts. An author declaration rendered for transparency — compare `chunk_count`, which is measured from the uploaded containers, to spot a release claiming less than it touches. `changes` is null for archives predating the format.

302.description: Signed code-mod artifact; redirect to its canonical URL.

get.summary: Published releases that claim any of the same chunks
get.description: Two content releases conflict exactly when their IoStore containers claim at least one chunk ID in common; whichever mounts later wins those chunks. Computed from the uploaded containers, not from author declarations.

post.summary: Conflict matrix for a set of releases
post.description: The endpoint mod managers integrate against: given the releases a profile intends to install, returns every pair that claims the same chunk. An empty list means any load order works.

get.description: Approved screenshots and videos. A signed-in caller also gets their own pending and rejected submissions, marked by `status`; moderators see everything.

post.summary: Submit a screenshot or video to a mod's gallery
post.description: multipart/form-data with `file` (png/jpeg/webp ≤ 8 MiB, or mp4/webm ≤ 64 MiB) and `alt_text` (required — every item ships with a description). Any signed-in account may submit; the item stays `pending` and invisible to others until a moderator approves it. Moderator submissions publish immediately.

201.description: The stored item, with its moderation status.

400.description: Missing alt text, unsupported file, or a full gallery.

get.description: Approved screenshots and videos for one of the tools on /tools. Moderators additionally see anything not yet approved.

post.summary: Add a preview to a tool (moderators)
post.description: multipart/form-data with `file` (png/jpeg/webp ≤ 8 MiB, or mp4/webm ≤ 64 MiB) and `alt_text` (required — every item ships with a description). Moderators only, and the item publishes immediately: there is no queue for a gallery only moderators can write to.

400.description: Missing alt text, unsupported file, or a full gallery.

delete.description: The uploader, the mod's owner, or a moderator. A tool preview has no owner, so it is the uploader or a moderator.

get.description: Streams the image or video. Byte ranges are honoured so videos can seek. Items not yet approved are served only to their uploader and moderators; everyone else gets 404, not 403 — the queue's existence is nobody else's business.

put.description: One rating per user per mod; calling again replaces yours.

get.description: Flat list, oldest first; `parent_id` links replies. Clients assemble the tree.

delete.description: Author or moderator. Soft delete: the thread keeps its shape, the body is blanked.

get.description: The authenticated account, for tools that need to embed their own identity — the tag editor puts it in signed release statements.

post.description: Binds an Ed25519 public key to your account. Idempotent for a key you already registered. A key belongs to exactly one account, ever.

400.description: Bad key, or too many keys.

409.description: Key belongs to another account, or was revoked.

delete.description: Future uploads signed with this key are rejected. Releases it already signed keep their history; yank those separately if needed.

post.description: Keys are created from a browser session only — a key cannot mint more keys. The full key appears once in the response and never again.

get.description: Mods pulled from public view — automatically by report volume, or by a moderator — each with its open-report tally so the queue can be worked without cross-referencing.

post.summary: Restore, hide, or remove a mod (moderators)
post.description: `restore` returns a hidden mod to public view, `hide` pulls a published one pending review, `remove` takes it down for good. Every decision lands in the audit log.

404.description: No such mod, or not in a state the action applies to.

post.summary: Approve or reject a gallery submission (moderators)
post.description: Approval publishes the item to the mod's gallery. Rejection keeps the record (and the bytes, visible only to the uploader) so the submitter can see what happened and delete it themselves.
Owner or moderator. A yanked release stops being downloadable and leaves the conflict index, but its record and scan history remain.

get.description: Every account that has signed in, with its Discord snowflake. `q` matches a Discord ID exactly, or the Discord username / display name as a substring; empty lists the newest signups.

200.description: Matching accounts, newest first, plus the match count.

post.summary: Mirror the signed code-mod set onto hub pages
post.description: Fetches the latest signed release manifest, verifies its Ed25519 signature against the platform's committed public key, and upserts a hub mod page and release per entry. Idempotent; callable by anyone because the signature, not the caller, is the authority. CI calls it after every code-mods release.

502.description: Manifest unreachable, unparseable, or its signature failed.
